## Quick quiz

Answer by instinct. No air resistance.

::: {.mcq-set data-mode="pretest"}

::: {.mcq}
A feather and a piano fall from $100\ \text{m}$. Which lands first?

- the piano
- the piano, by a little
- ✓ same time

::: {.sol}
No air: landing speed depends on height, not on mass.
:::
:::

::: {.mcq}
A car at $50\ \text{km/h}$ stops in $14\ \text{m}$. At $100\ \text{km/h}$, how many metres to stop?

- $14\ \text{m}$
- $28\ \text{m}$
- ✓ $56\ \text{m}$

::: {.sol}
Energy × 4, so distance × 4.
:::
:::

::: {.mcq}
Two balls leave a window at the same speed: one down, one up. Which lands faster?

- the one thrown down
- the one thrown up
- ✓ same speed

::: {.sol}
Same energy at the start, same energy at the end.
:::
:::

:::

## Three formulas

```{=html}
<div class="vf">
 <div class="cards">
  <div class="card" style="--c:#EF9F27"><div class="nm">Kinetic energy</div><div class="fm">E<sub>k</sub> = ½ m v²</div><div class="pr">E<sub>k</sub> ∝ v²</div><div class="ex">∝ means directly proportional: double the speed, 4 × the energy.</div></div>
  <div class="card" style="--c:#1D9E75"><div class="nm">Gravitational potential energy</div><div class="fm">ΔE<sub>p</sub> = m g Δh</div><div class="pr">ΔE<sub>p</sub> ∝ Δh</div><div class="ex">Twice as high, twice the energy.</div></div>
  <div class="card" style="--c:#888780"><div class="nm">Work</div><div class="fm">W = F × d</div><div class="pr">W ∝ F and W ∝ d</div><div class="ex">Force along the motion, times the distance moved.</div></div>
 </div>
 <p class="note">All three are measured in joules (J), but they are not the same thing: kinetic and potential energy are <b>stores</b>, work is a <b>transfer</b>.</p>
 <h4>When are they equal?</h4>
 <div class="row"><span class="when">Braking</span><span class="fm">E<sub>k</sub> = W = F × d</span><span class="ex">All the motion store becomes work done by the brakes.</span></div>
 <div class="row"><span class="when">Thrown up, or falling</span><span class="fm">E<sub>k</sub> = ΔE<sub>p</sub></span><span class="ex">Motion store and height store swap, with no air resistance.</span></div>
 <div class="row"><span class="when">Lifted slowly, or pushed by gravity</span><span class="fm">ΔE<sub>p</sub> = W</span><span class="ex">The work done is the height store gained or lost: W = m g Δh.</span></div>
</div>
```

## Check yourself

::: {.mcq-set}

::: {.mcq}
Speed × 3. Kinetic energy:

- × 3
- × 6
- ✓ × 9
- × 12

::: {.sol}
$3^2 = 9$
:::
:::

::: {.mcq}
Box of $3\ \text{kg}$, shelf from $0.5\ \text{m}$ to $1.5\ \text{m}$. Gain in potential energy:

- $15\ \text{J}$
- ✓ $30\ \text{J}$
- $45\ \text{J}$
- $450\ \text{J}$

::: {.sol}
$m g \Delta h = 3 \times 10 \times 1 = 30\ \text{J}$
:::
:::

::: {.mcq}
Book of $2\ \text{kg}$ lifted $1.2\ \text{m}$: straight up, or along a ramp. Gain in potential energy:

- bigger on the ramp
- smaller on the ramp
- ✓ the same: $24\ \text{J}$
- $0\ \text{J}$

::: {.sol}
Only $\Delta h$ counts, not the path.
:::
:::

::: {.mcq}
Push $120\ \text{N}$ over $5\ \text{m}$. Work:

- $24\ \text{J}$
- $125\ \text{J}$
- ✓ $600\ \text{J}$
- $4800\ \text{J}$

::: {.sol}
$W = F d = 600\ \text{J}$
:::
:::

::: {.mcq}
Speed × 2, same brakes. Stopping distance:

- ÷ 2
- × 2
- ✓ × 4
- same

::: {.sol}
$E_k$ × 4, so $d$ × 4.
:::
:::

::: {.mcq}
Wet road: half the braking force. Stopping distance:

- ÷ 2
- same
- ✓ × 2
- × 4

::: {.sol}
$d = E_k / F$: half $F$, double $d$.
:::
:::

:::

## For those who want the numbers

Worked example, practice, and an exam-style sheet. Use $g = 10\ \text{N/kg}$.

### Worked example

A ball of $0.20\ \text{kg}$ is dropped from $1.8\ \text{m}$. Speed at the ground? No air.

**Data.** $m = 0.20\ \text{kg}$, $\Delta h = 1.8\ \text{m}$.

**Energy.** $\Delta E_p = m g \Delta h = 0.20 \times 10 \times 1.8 = 3.6\ \text{J}$. All of it becomes $E_k$.

**Speed.** $\tfrac12 \times 0.20 \times v^2 = 3.6$, so $v^2 = 36$ and $v = 6.0\ \text{m/s}$ (about $22\ \text{km/h}$).

**Check.** Units are J and m/s. $6\ \text{m/s}$ is a fast run: plausible. A heavier ball? Same speed: $m$ cancels in $m g \Delta h = \tfrac12 m v^2$.

### Practice

**1.** A ball of $0.50\ \text{kg}$ moves at $8.0\ \text{m/s}$. (a) Kinetic energy? (b) Thrown at $16\ \text{m/s}$: kinetic energy, and compared with (a)? (c) Cyclist and bike, $75\ \text{kg}$, at $36\ \text{km/h}$: kinetic energy?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
(a) $\tfrac12 \times 0.50 \times 8.0^2 = 16\ \text{J}$. (b) $\tfrac12 \times 0.50 \times 16^2 = 64\ \text{J}$: 4 × more, since speed doubled. (c) $36 \div 3.6 = 10\ \text{m/s}$, so $E_k = \tfrac12 \times 75 \times 10^2 = 3750\ \text{J}$.
:::

**2.** (a) A climber of $60\ \text{kg}$ gains $200\ \text{m}$ of height: gain in potential energy? (b) A stone of $0.10\ \text{kg}$ is thrown up at $12\ \text{m/s}$: how high above the hand? No air.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
(a) $60 \times 10 \times 200 = 120\,000\ \text{J} = 120\ \text{kJ}$. (b) $E_k = \tfrac12 \times 0.10 \times 12^2 = 7.2\ \text{J}$. At the top it is all $E_p$: $7.2 = 0.10 \times 10 \times \Delta h$, so $\Delta h = 7.2\ \text{m}$.
:::

**3.** (a) A crate of $40\ \text{kg}$ is pushed $5.0\ \text{m}$ with $120\ \text{N}$: work done? (b) You carry a bag of $20\ \text{kg}$ for $10\ \text{m}$ at constant speed, level: work done by your upward force? (c) Cyclist and bike, $80\ \text{kg}$, at $6.0\ \text{m/s}$, brake with $120\ \text{N}$: stopping distance? And at $12\ \text{m/s}$?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
(a) $W = F d = 600\ \text{J}$. Mass not needed. (b) $0\ \text{J}$: the force is up, the motion is sideways. (c) $E_k = \tfrac12 \times 80 \times 6.0^2 = 1440\ \text{J}$, so $d = 1440 / 120 = 12\ \text{m}$. At $12\ \text{m/s}$: $E_k = 5760\ \text{J}$, $d = 48\ \text{m}$: 4 × more.
:::

### Exam-style sheet

$g = 10\ \text{N/kg}$. Show every step, give units. Total: 33 marks.

**1 · Kinetic energy (4).** Cyclist and bike, $80\ \text{kg}$, at $36\ \text{km/h}$. (a) Speed in $\text{m/s}$. (b) Kinetic energy. (c) Speed doubles: $E_k$ changes by what factor?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
(a) $10\ \text{m/s}$. (b) $\tfrac12 \times 80 \times 10^2 = 4000\ \text{J}$. (c) × 4 ($16\,000\ \text{J}$). Common slips: $36$ instead of $10$ (51 840 J), no square (400 J), no $\tfrac12$ (8000 J).
:::

**2 · Potential energy (3).** A book of $1.5\ \text{kg}$ is lifted from the floor to a shelf $2.0\ \text{m}$ high. (a) Gain in potential energy. (b) It is then pushed $3.0\ \text{m}$ along the shelf: change in $E_p$? Explain.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
(a) $1.5 \times 10 \times 2.0 = 30\ \text{J}$. (b) $0\ \text{J}$: $\Delta h = 0$. The push ends up as thermal energy (friction).
:::

**3 · Speed and energy (4).** A car of $1200\ \text{kg}$ drives $90\ \text{km}$ at $72\ \text{km/h}$. (a) Time in minutes. (b) Kinetic energy.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
(a) $90 / 72 = 1.25\ \text{h} = 75\ \text{min}$. (b) $72 \div 3.6 = 20\ \text{m/s}$, so $E_k = \tfrac12 \times 1200 \times 20^2 = 240\,000\ \text{J}$.
:::

**4 · Roller coaster (5).** A trolley of $400\ \text{kg}$ starts at rest at A, $20\ \text{m}$ high. B is $5\ \text{m}$ high, C is at ground level. No friction. (a) $E_p$ lost from A to B. (b) $E_k$ and speed at B. (c) Speed at C.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
(a) $400 \times 10 \times 15 = 60\,000\ \text{J}$. (b) $E_k = 60\,000\ \text{J}$, so $v = \sqrt{2 \times 60\,000 / 400} = \sqrt{300} = 17.3\ \text{m/s}$. (c) $E_k = 400 \times 10 \times 20 = 80\,000\ \text{J}$, so $v = \sqrt{400} = 20\ \text{m/s}$. Energies add up from A, speeds do not.
:::

**5 · Work (4).** A student pushes a box of $25\ \text{kg}$ along a level floor with a constant horizontal force of $60\ \text{N}$. It moves $8.0\ \text{m}$ at constant speed. (a) Work done by the student. (b) Friction force, and why. (c) The box gains no kinetic energy: where does the energy go?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
(a) $60 \times 8.0 = 480\ \text{J}$. Mass not needed. (b) $60\ \text{N}$: constant speed, so the forces balance. (c) Into the thermal store of box and floor (friction), then it spreads out.
:::

**6 · The ramp (4).** A crate of $50\ \text{kg}$ is pushed up a $4.0\ \text{m}$ ramp with $150\ \text{N}$ parallel to the ramp. It rises $1.0\ \text{m}$. (a) Work done. (b) Gain in potential energy. (c) How much work is not stored as $E_p$, and where does it go?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
(a) $150 \times 4.0 = 600\ \text{J}$ (distance along the ramp). (b) $50 \times 10 \times 1.0 = 500\ \text{J}$ (height counts). (c) $100\ \text{J}$, to the thermal store by friction.
:::

**7 · Stopping a truck (5).** A truck of $8000\ \text{kg}$ at $54\ \text{km/h}$ brakes with a constant $30\,000\ \text{N}$. (a) Kinetic energy. (b) Stopping distance. (c) At twice the speed: distance? Explain, no full calculation.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
(a) $54 \div 3.6 = 15\ \text{m/s}$, so $E_k = \tfrac12 \times 8000 \times 15^2 = 900\,000\ \text{J}$. (b) $d = 900\,000 / 30\,000 = 30\ \text{m}$. (c) $120\ \text{m}$: $E_k \propto v^2$ and $d \propto E_k$, so × 4, not × 2.
:::

**8 · A falling ball (4).** A ball of $0.50\ \text{kg}$ is dropped from $45\ \text{m}$. No air. (a) $E_p$ lost. (b) $E_k$ just before landing. (c) Speed in $\text{m/s}$ and in $\text{km/h}$.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
(a) $0.50 \times 10 \times 45 = 225\ \text{J}$. (b) $225\ \text{J}$. (c) $v = \sqrt{2 \times 225 / 0.50} = \sqrt{900} = 30\ \text{m/s}$, and $30 \times 3.6 = 108\ \text{km/h}$.
:::

### Spot the mistake

A car of $1000\ \text{kg}$ at $50\ \text{km/h}$ has $E_k \approx 97\ \text{kJ}$. Three slips that still give a number that looks fine:

- Speed in $\text{km/h}$: $1\,250\,000\ \text{J}$, about 13 × too big.
- No square: $6950\ \text{J}$.
- No $\tfrac12$: $193\,000\ \text{J}$, double.

Three checks: **units** (J, m/s), **size** (compare with a known case, like the 97 kJ), **ratio** (speed × 2 means energy × 4).
